title: My home
goal: Name the rooms and furniture in your home, and say what there is and isn't with il y a and il n'y a pas de.

items.fr: il y a / il n'y a pas de
items.en: there is / there are, and there isn't / there aren't any

drills.text: Dans le salon, ___ un canapé et une table.
drills.en: In the living room, there's a sofa and a table.
drills.explain: [[Il y a]] means both “there is” and “there are”.
[[Il y a]] never changes, even for plurals.

drills.prompt: “There are no chairs in the kitchen.” Which is correct?
options: Il n'y a pas de chaises dans la cuisine.
Il n'y a pas des chaises dans la cuisine.
Il y a pas les chaises dans la cuisine.
drills.explain: Negative + [[de]]: [[il n'y a pas de chaises]].

example.fr: J'habite dans un appartement de trois pièces.
example.en: I live in a three-room apartment.

example.fr: Mes parents habitent dans une grande maison.
example.en: My parents live in a big house.

items.note: The general word. A bedroom is [[une chambre]].
Also written [[salle de bain]], especially in Québec.
For the room, France uses the plural [[les toilettes]]. In Québec, [[la toilette]] (singular) is very common: it means the toilet itself, and people also use it for the room.
The t is silent: [[lit]] sounds like “lee”.
In Québec, [[le divan]] is very common too.

blocks.title: Amira shows Lucie her new apartment in Montréal
blocks.context: Amira has just moved. Her friend Lucie comes to visit.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui ! C'est un quatre et demie. Il y a une cuisine, un salon, deux chambres et une salle de bains.
lines.en: Yes! It's a 4 ½. There's a kitchen, a living room, two bedrooms and a bathroom.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, il y a un petit balcon. Mais il n'y a pas de canapé dans le salon !
lines.en: Yes, there's a small balcony. But there's no sofa in the living room!

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Pas de canapé ? Et les toilettes ?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Les toilettes sont dans la salle de bains.
lines.en: The toilet is in the bathroom.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Ma chambre est grande. Il y a un lit, une table et une chaise. C'est simple, mais j'aime beaucoup mon appartement.
lines.en: My bedroom is big. There's a bed, a table and a chair. It's simple, but I really like my apartment.

blocks.title: Olivier's apartment in Lyon
blocks.fr: J'habite à Lyon, en France. Mon appartement est petit : c'est un appartement de deux pièces. Il y a un salon, une chambre, une petite cuisine et une salle de bains. Il n'y a pas de balcon.
blocks.en: I live in Lyon, in France. My apartment is small: it's a two-room apartment. There's a living room, a bedroom, a small kitchen and a bathroom. There's no balcony.

blocks.body: Listen first. Count the rooms in each home. Amira says she has a “4 ½” and Olivier says “two rooms”: the deep dive in the next step explains why the numbers are so different.

steps.title: Rooms, furniture and il y a

blocks.title: Pièce or chambre?
blocks.body:
[[Une pièce]] is **any room** in a home: the kitchen, the living room, a bedroom. [[Une chambre]] is only a **bedroom**.

So [[un appartement de trois pièces]] is a three-room apartment, and [[Il y a deux chambres]] means there are two bedrooms. English speakers often say [[chambre]] for every room: try to avoid that.

blocks.title: There is, there are: il y a
blocks.pattern: il y a + un / une / des + nom
blocks.note: [[Il y a]] is a fixed chunk. It means **there is** and **there are**, and it never changes for plurals. To ask a question, just raise your voice at the end: [[Il y a un balcon ?]]

examples.fr: Il y a des chaises dans la cuisine.
examples.en: There are chairs in the kitchen.

blocks.title: Saying what there isn't
head: il y a…
il n'y a pas…
English
rows: Il n'y a pas de balcon.
Il n'y a pas de table.
Il n'y a pas de chaises.
blocks.note: You know this from food: after a negative, [[un]], [[une]], [[des]] (and [[du]], [[de la]]) all become **[[de]]**, or **[[d']]** before a vowel. [[Ne]] becomes [[n']] before [[y]]: [[il n'y a pas]].

blocks.body:
- **Il y a does not change:** it has no plural form: [[Il y a trois chambres]], [[Il y a des chaises]].
- **Il y a vs il a:** [[Il y a un lit]] = there is a bed. [[Il a un lit]] = he has a bed. The little [[y]] matters!
- **Pas de, not pas un:** [[Il n'y a pas de canapé]], not [[Il n'y a pas un canapé]].
- **Toilets are plural in France:** [[les toilettes sont…]], with a plural verb.

blocks.title: What is a “4 ½”?
blocks.body:
In Québec, apartments are named by counting the rooms: the kitchen, the living room and each bedroom count as one, and the **bathroom counts as a half**. So:

- [[un trois et demie]] (3 ½) = kitchen, living room, one bedroom, bathroom
- [[un quatre et demie]] (4 ½) = kitchen, living room, two bedrooms, bathroom
- [[un cinq et demie]] (5 ½) = kitchen, living room, three bedrooms, bathroom

In ads you see “4 ½” or “4 1/2”. Out loud, people say [[un quatre et demie]]; you will also see it written [[quatre et demi]]. Both spellings occur; this course uses [[demie]].

In France, people count only the main rooms (living room and bedrooms), not the kitchen or bathroom: [[un appartement de trois pièces]] or [[un trois-pièces]] has a living room and two bedrooms. So a Montréal 4 ½ and a Paris three-room apartment can be the same size!

Also in Québec: [[le divan]] for the sofa, [[la salle de bain]] (singular), and often [[la toilette]] (singular) for the toilet or the toilet room, where France says [[les toilettes]].

examples.fr: J'habite dans un quatre et demie.
examples.en: I live in a 4 ½ (two-bedroom apartment).

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: Say it as one quick chunk: “eel-yah”. In fast speech it often shrinks to “yah”.

lines.fr: Il n'y a pas de balcon.
lines.tip: Say “eel-nyah-pah-duh”. The n of balcon is nasal, not pronounced.
[[bains]] rhymes with [[vin]]; the s is silent.
Link the words: the n of un is heard, “un-nappartement”.

lines.fr: J'habite dans un appartement de trois pièces.
lines.en: I live in a three-room apartment.

blocks.explain: [[chambres]] = bedrooms. A room in general is [[une pièce]].

blocks.fr: Il n'y a pas de canapé dans le salon.
blocks.en: There's no sofa in the living room.
blocks.prompt: What's missing in the living room?
blocks.explain: [[Il n'y a pas de canapé]]: there's no sofa.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Getting something wrong now helps you remember it later.

blocks.en: In my apartment, there are two bedrooms.
blocks.explain: “There are” = [[il y a]], even for plurals.

blocks.prompt: How do you say “There's no sofa”?
options: Il n'y a pas de canapé.
Il n'y a pas un canapé.
optionFeedback: After a negative, un becomes de.
Il n'a pas de canapé means “he doesn't have a sofa”: the y is missing.
Être is not used here: you need il y a.

blocks.prompt: There's a big bed in the bedroom.
accept: Il y a un grand lit dans la chambre.
Dans la chambre, il y a un grand lit.
blocks.explain: [[Il y a]] + [[un grand lit]]; [[grand]] comes before the noun, like [[petit]].

blocks.text: Il n'y a pas ___ chaises dans la cuisine.
blocks.en: There are no chairs in the kitchen.

blocks.prompt: I live in a three-room apartment.
accept: J'habite dans un appartement de trois pièces.
blocks.explain: [[un appartement de trois pièces]]: the number of rooms comes after [[de]].

blocks.prompt: Raj's bedroom is small. Which is correct?
blocks.explain: [[chambre]] is feminine: [[sa chambre]], and the adjective takes -e: [[petite]].
optionFeedback: Chambre is feminine: sa, not son.
The adjective agrees with chambre (feminine): petite.

accept: Est-ce qu'il y a un balcon ?
blocks.explain: Use [[il y a]] with a rising voice: [[Il y a un balcon ?]]

blocks.fr: Il y a un canapé dans le salon.
accept: Il y a un canapé dans le salon
blocks.explain: [[canapé]] ends with é; the n of [[salon]] is nasal.

blocks.prompt: A new friend asks about your home. Describe it: house or apartment, how many rooms, what there is, and one thing there isn't.
checklist: J'habite dans un appartement / une maison
Il y a + at least three rooms

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: J'habite dans un appartement à Gatineau. C'est un quatre et demie. Il y a une cuisine, un salon, deux chambres et une salle de bains. Dans ma chambre, il y a un grand lit et une chaise. Il y a un balcon, mais il n'y a pas de canapé !
models.en: I live in an apartment in Gatineau. It's a 4 ½. There's a kitchen, a living room, two bedrooms and a bathroom. In my bedroom there's a big bed and a chair. There's a balcony, but there's no sofa!

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to a friend about your home: the type of home, the rooms, and what there is (and isn't) in one room.
checklist: List the rooms with il y a
Use il n'y a pas de at least once
Use mon / ma for your rooms

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Alex ! Maintenant, j'habite dans un quatre et demie à Montréal. Il y a une grande cuisine, un salon et deux chambres. Il n'y a pas de balcon. Ma chambre est petite, mais j'aime beaucoup mon appartement ! À bientôt, Mei
models.en: Hi Alex! Now I live in a 4 ½ in Montréal. There's a big kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms. There's no balcony. My bedroom is small, but I really like my apartment! See you soon, Mei

summary:
- Name the rooms of a home and the main furniture, with their gender
- Say what there is with [[il y a]] and what there isn't with [[il n'y a pas de]]
- Describe your home: [[J'habite dans un appartement de trois pièces.]]
- Understand a Québec “4 ½”
